Distribution and ecology: — Currently, the species is known from only three localities, two of them located in the districts of Huancabamba [L. Valenzuela et al. 13849 (HOXA) and J. Perea et al. 890 (MO)] and Chontabamba [L. Valenzuela & A. Peña 13880 (HOXA)] between 2000 - 3000 m elevation, in the province of Oxapampa, Pasco department (Figure 5). These localities are located within the Oxapampa-Asháninka-Yánesha Biosphere Reserve (BIOAY), which is characterized by montane forests that form an immense strip of vegetation. These ecosystems are mostly humid, shaded, with rugged topography and basically white sandy soil, with frequent rainfall in all seasons of the year, accompanied by continuous fog and variable temperatures, ranging from warm, temperate, cold, and even very cold, with significant differences throughout the year (Catchpole 2004, Valenzuela-Gamarra et al. 2022). Pleurothallis yanesha grows as an epiphytic or rarely terrestrial (Figure 6), forming small colonies of 4 – 6 individuals, sharing its habitat with other plant species, mainly trees such as Clusia alata Planchón & Triana (1860: 361), Clusia trochiformis Vesque (1893: 49), Escallonia myrtilloides Linnaeus (1781: 156), Ocotea pajonalis van der Werff (2013: 354), Posoqueria coriacea Martens & Galeotti (1844: 240), Saracha punctata Ruiz & Pavón (1799: 42), Symplocos nana Brand (1901: 76), in sympatry with other orchid species such as Epidendrum geminiochraceum Hágsater, Santiago & Medina (2019: 1725), Scaphosepalum atropurpureum Valenzuela (2015: 339), Sobralia caloglossa Schlechter (1929: 31), and Zootrophion dayanum Luer (1982: 82). Flowering of this species occurs between October and November, in the beginning of the wet season.
